lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCada ciclo repite: \u:
"

Each cycle repeats: (1) oxidation with FAD (FADH₂); (2) hydration; (3) oxidation with NAD⁺ (NADH); (4) thiolysis, which releases a unit of acetyl-CoA (2 C) and leaves an acyl-CoA two carbons shorter. It repeats until only acetyl-CoA remains. Choose the chain length and advance.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl glutamato libera \:
"

Glutamate releases NH₄⁺ (glutamate dehydrogenase), which is toxic and which the liver converts into urea in the urea cycle (consumes 4 high-energy bonds) and is excreted in the urine. Carbon skeletons are classified as glucogenic (give pyruvate or other Krebs intermediates → glucose) and ketogenic (give acetyl-CoA or acetoacetate → ketone bodies). Select the amino acid to see its fate.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el citosol la \u00:
"

In the cytosol acyl-CoA synthetase activates the fatty acid (RCOO⁻ + CoA + ATP → acyl-CoA + AMP + PPᵢ; 2 high-energy bonds are spent). The inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to acyl-CoA: CPT-I converts it into acyl-carnitine, which enters through a translocase and CPT-II regenerates it in the matrix. CPT-I is the control point (inhibited by malonyl-CoA).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos \u003cb\u003etria:
"

Triacylglycerols are the most concentrated energy reserve (≈ 37 kJ/g versus ≈ 17 kJ/g for carbohydrates): they are highly reduced and stored without water. Lipases release fatty acids and glycerol; the fatty acids are oxidized in the mitochondrial matrix by β-oxidation, and amino acids are degraded after removal of the amino group.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePara degradar un amin:
"

To degrade an amino acid the amino group is removed first: an aminotransferase with pyridoxal phosphate (PLP, vitamin B₆) transfers the –NH₂ group to α-ketoglutarate, which forms glutamate, and the amino acid becomes its α-keto acid. It is a reversible reaction. Amino acids end up collecting their amino group in glutamate.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn ácido graso satura:
"

A saturated fatty acid of n carbons (n even) requires n/2 − 1 cycles and produces n/2 acetyl-CoA (10 ATP each in the Krebs cycle), n/2 − 1 FADH₂ (1.5 ATP) and n/2 − 1 NADH (2.5 ATP); 2 ATP are subtracted for activation: ATP = 7n − 6. For palmitate (C16): 106 ATP. With excess acetyl-CoA the liver forms ketone bodies.

"
